pages.text: Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 Skip Navigation Within Census Bureau Library Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 April 16, 2026 Written by: ROSS JACOBSON, JAMI SEGAL, JENNIFER WENNING, and SEAN WILBURN Report Number: G25-ASPEP Introduction Download Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 [PDF - <1.0 MB] In March 2025, state and local governments employed 20.3 million people, an increase of 1.4 percent from the 2024 figure of 20.0 million. Nationally, local government workers comprised the majority of the state and local government workforce with 14.7 million employees (72.2 percent). In comparison, state governments employed 5.7 million workers (27.8 percent). Of the total 20.3 million employed, 15.8 million were classified as full-time and 4.5 million as part-time. Full-time employment by state governments increased by 2.7 percent to 4.1 million, while full-time employment by local governments increased 1.2 percent to 11.7 million. The number of part-time state government employees increased 0.8 percent to 1.5 million. Part-time local government employees increased 0.8 percent to 3.0 million. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Ant Hills WSA | Colorado View Map In Full Screen The remote Ant Hills Wilderness Study Area (WSA) consists of hills and valleys on the southern slopes of Douglas Mountain, which trend southward into Dinosaur National Monument and the Yampa River. The Ant Hills consist of several hills rising 400 to 500 feet above the draws in the southeastern part of the WSA. The area is an extension of the landforms and upper end of drainages found in Dinosaur National Monument. There are no developed recreation sites in the Douglas Mountain area, but the area offers opportunities for visitors to enjoy deer and elk hunting, camping, sightseeing, hiking, backpacking and horseback riding. Motorized and mechanized vehicle travel is limited to existing roads and trails within these WSAs. Vegetation consists mainly of ponderosa pine, pinyon-juniper woodlands, sagebrush, and native grass communities. Fauna includes mule deer, elk, raptors and other birds, and various small mammals and reptiles. pages.text: Antecedentes | Naciones Unidas Skip to main content UNICEF/Karel Prinsloo ¿Qué es el Día Mundial del Retrete? El Día Mundial del Retrete se conmemora todos los años el 19 de noviembre con el objetivo de generar conciencia y promover la adopción de medidas encaminadas a la consecución del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 6 (ODS 6): “garantizar la disponibilidad y la gestión sostenible del agua y el saneamiento para todos”. Millones de personas y organizaciones de todo el mundo participan en la campaña del Día Mundial del Retrete, coordinada por ONU-Agua, a través de distintas actividades de difusión, iniciativas y eventos. ¿Por qué son importantes los retretes? El saneamiento es un derecho humano. Sin embargo, miles de millones de personas siguen sin tener acceso a retretes seguros, lo que tiene consecuencias devastadoras para su salud, educación y medios de subsistencia, así como para el medio ambiente. La crisis mundial del saneamiento nos afecta a todos, aunque de forma desigual. Las mujeres y las niñas, así como otros grupos vulnerables, son quienes más sufren sus consecuencias. ¿Qué está haciendo la ONU para contribuir a que todo el mundo tenga acceso a retretes seguros? Una de las metas del ODS 6 es lograr que, de aquí a 2030, todas las personas tengan acceso a servicios de saneamiento e higiene gestionados sin riesgos, “prestando especial atención a las necesidades de las mujeres y las niñas y de las personas en situaciones de vulnerabilidad”. pages.text: Anthony Onnembo beat cancer, played at Nike RBI World Series Skip to Content Before his life changed forever, Anthony Onnembo was an eighth grader in New Jersey who made a commitment to himself that he was going to make the varsity baseball team at Northern Valley Regional High School his freshman year. “I trained like an absolute animal to get there,” Onnembo said. “I was 100% all gas, no brakes. Everything towards it, and then in December of my freshman year I was diagnosed with pediatric follicular lymphoma. A lymphoma so rare that it wasn't even recognized [until] 2016.” Now 18, Onnembo spent his final youth summer baseball tournament at the Jackie Robinson Training Complex for the Nike RBI World Series . He arrived in Vero Beach, Fla., as a cancer survivor and a published author. He later left as the winner of the Nike RBI “Breaking Barriers” essay competition with his story. What kept him centered through three relapses, multiple surgeries, chemotherapy, radiation and misdiagnoses was baseball. For more than three and a half years, Onnembo lived with his diagnosis in secret. The only people at his school who knew were his coach, one administrator and a nurse. “I didn't want anyone to fear for me,” said Onnembo, who learned he had cancer when he was 14 years old. “I didn't want anyone to worry for me.” Anthony Onnembo during the 2026 Nike RBI Senior Baseball World Series at Jackie Robinson Training Complex on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, in Vero Beach, Fla. Antibody Seroprevalence Sept. 5, 2025 Español At a glance Antibodies are proteins that your immune system makes to help fight infection and protect you from getting sick in the future. Antibodies to SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, can be detected in the blood of people who have recovered from COVID-19 or people who have been vaccinated against COVID-19. Antibodies and COVID-19 Some people with antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 may become infected after vaccination (vaccine breakthrough infection) or after recovering from a past infection (reinfected). When reinfections or breakthrough infections happen, having antibodies plays an important role in helping prevent severe illness, hospitalization, and death. For many diseases, including COVID-19, antibodies are expected to decrease or "wane" over time. As antibodies wane, you may become more vulnerable to severe illness. pages.text: Antique Road Show Skip to main content The fabled road (a c. 1955 postcard) stretched 2,448 miles. National Museum of American History, Transportation Collection, Smithsonian Institution Back when the Model A Ford was America's ticket to ride, it must have seemed that half the nation was heading west on Route 66. In fact, the late songwriter Bobby Troup penned "Get Your Kicks on Route 66" during his own trip west on that legendary highway just after World War II, not only launching a songwriting career but also placing the road in the mythos of America. Those who took to the highway in the 1930s to escape drought in the Midwest and cross the desert to California might have been more inclined, if you'll allow me a complete anachronism, to hum a few bars of the hard-rock classic "Highway to Hell." What it was, more accurately, was a highway from hell, with the hope of a paradise at the western end of a paved rainbow. In today's age of major four- and six-lane thoroughfares to and from just about everywhere, it's not easy to conceive just how powerfully one stretch of two-lane highway could grip America's collective imagination. This country has historically looked west for a better tomorrow—Daniel Boone and his fellow woodsmen headed for the setting sun as soon as they could see three or four cabins from their homesteads. So when Henry Ford began producing affordable cars, and the Federal Highway Act of 1921 led to the linking of rural roads, a great convergence took place. pages.text: AR- Say #NoToHate - آثار خطاب الكراهية والإجراءات التي يمكنك اتخاذها | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content #لا_للكراهية خطاب الكراهية آخذ في التصاعد في جميع أنحاء العالم يحرض خطاب الكراهية على العنف والتعصب. وليس التأثير المدمر للكراهية بأمر جديد للأسف. غير أن نطاق الكراهية وتأثيرها تعاظما اليوم بفعل تقانات الاتصال الجديدة. فقد أصبح خطاب الكراهية، بما في ذلك خطاب الكراهية على الإنترنت، من أكثر السبل شيوعا لنشر الخطاب المثير للانقسام على نطاق عالمي، بما يهدد السلام في أنحاء العالم. للأمم المتحدة تاريخ طويل في حشد العالم ضد الكراهية بجميع أنواعها للدفاع عن حقوق الإنسان والنهوض بسيادة القانون . ويمتد تأثير خطاب الكراهية عبر عديد مجالات العمل التي تركز عليها الأمم المتحدة، من حماية حقوق الإنسان ومنع الفظائع إلى صون السلام وتحقيق المساواة بين الجنسين ودعم الأطفال والشباب. لأن مكافحة الكراهية والتمييز والعنصرية وغياب المساواة تقع في صميم مبادئ الأمم المتحدة الأساسية، تعمل المنظمة على التصدي لخطاب الكراهية في كل منعطف. وقد أُرسيت هذه المهمة في ميثاق الأمم المتحدة ، وفي الأطر الدولية لحقوق الإنسان، وفي الجهود العالمية الرامية إلى تحقيق أهداف التنمية المستدامة . ليست كلماتي: الممثل الذي يحمل صوت الإبادة الجماعية خطاب الكراهية جرس إنذار ، فكلما تعالى صوته، اشتد خطر الإبادة الجماعية. إنه يسبق العنف ويغذيه.” أنطونيو غوتيريش ، الأمين العام للأمم المتحدة استراتيجية وخطة عمل الأمم المتحدة بشأن خطاب الكراهية استجابة للاتجاهات المثيرة للقلق المتمثلة في تزايد كراهية الأجانب والعنصرية والتعصب وكراهية النساء العنيفة ومعاداة السامية وكراهية المسلمين في أنحاء العالم، دشن الأمين العام للأمم المتحدة أنطونيو غوتيريش استراتيجية وخطة عمل الأمم المتحدة بشأن خطاب الكراهية في 18 حَزيران/يونيه 2019. وتتيح

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Aravaipa Canyon Wilderness | Arizona View Map In Full Screen With towering cliffs, flowing water and a rich diversity of flora and fauna, Aravaipa Canyon Wilderness remains as one of Arizona's truly unique areas. Its 19,410 acres of designated wilderness beckons adventurers who yearn for solitude and scenic splendor. Located in southeast Arizona, roughly between Tucson and Phoenix, the wilderness and surrounding public and private land conserve a vital ecosystem for future generations. Aravaipa Creek flows year-round, an unusual phenomenon in the Arizona desert. Nurtured by this abundant water, large sycamore, ash, cottonwood, and willow trees flourish along the stream, flanked by other riparian vegetation. In the fall, a kaleidoscope of brilliant red and golden leaves contrasts dramatically with the surrounding Sonoran Desert landscape. The Bureau of Land Management manages Aravaipa Canyon Wilderness to protect its essential wilderness character and fragile environment while providing the visitor with a world-class opportunity for primitive and unconfined recreation. pages.text: Archaeologists found 37 people buried in one giant 'death jar' | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE Archaeologists found 37 people buried in one giant 'death jar' A newly excavated megalithic container holding skeletal remains in Laos may help finally solve the mystery of the so-called "Plain of Jars." The discovery of bones and other artifacts inside a giant stone jar on the Xieng Khouang Plateau of Laos suggests the megalithic vessel may have served as a communal burial site for centuries. Daniel Baker By Meghie Rodrigues Published July 31, 2026 Located in northern Laos, the Xieng Khouang Plateau is home to one of the world's most puzzling archaeological sites: the Plain of Jars. The name comes from the hundreds of stone “jars” scattered around the area. For nearly a century, archaeologists have pondered their purpose, suspecting they were funerary urns, as some had been found with burnt bones and ashes. Now a team of researchers exploring the site has found a hefty, megalithic stone jar containing the remains of at least 37 people—from a toddler to adults—that dates to more than a thousand years ago. “We were very excited because it was the first time we found non-burnt bones inside a jar,” says Nicholas Skopal , an archaeologist at James Cook University in Australia and lead author of the study, which was published in spring in A ntiquity . The skeletal remains inside the jars were not tossed in randomly, Skopal says, as large bones and skulls were set near the outer edges. Comprising more than 280,000 artifacts, the finds—uncovered between modern-day Cambridge and Huntingdon —shed light on life in the region over roughly 12,000 years. But some discoveries raised more questions than answers: Why, for example, did a single ditch at the Bar Hill site in rural Cambridgeshire contain some 8,000 amphibian bones ?
